thread:
incident-bot: PAGE: High egress packet loss detected in eu-west-azc (region AZ-C). Alert group: network.egress.packet_loss > 5% for 2m. Severity: P1. @oncall
emma: I'm on it, grabbing logs and BGP. Starting triage. :eyes:
raj: Oncall here. Seeing customer error spikes and increased 5xx from frontend (eu). Which POPs are affected?
emma: Metrics: egress loss spike at azc-egress-1 and azc-egress-2. Health checks show some backend 502/503. Timeline ~ 2359000060 -> now.
oliver: I can run bgp dump and packet captures. Any suspected upstream provider?
emma: Preliminary RIB shows repeated withdraws from upstream ASN 64521 on our azc-facing sessions, causing traffic to reroute via eu-transit-b. Packet loss correlates with those flaps.
marta: Customer reports: chat with AcmeCorp CS - latency >2s and intermittent errors. Cust-success tagging impacted customers.
net-ops: Confirmed. We see BGP update churn with AS_PATH prepends and intermittent community changes. Looks like a churny neighbor, likely hardware flaps or misconfig.
emma: Quick evidence: applied curl to health endpoint on edge:
```
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" https://eu.api.redwood-inference.com/health
503 1.24
```
emma: tcpdump from azc-egress-1 showing retransmits and high RTOs. Attaching snippet below.
```
15:32:11.123456 IP 10.0.0.12 > 198.51.100.1: Flags [P.], seq 1:137, ack 1, win 229, length 136
15:32:11.223789 IP 198.51.100.1 > 10.0.0.12: Flags [R.], seq 1, ack 137, win 0, length 0
15:32:12.124000 IP 10.0.0.12 > 198.51.100.1: retransmission
```
raj: Noted. Emma, can you verify BGP session flaps count and adj-rib-in churn? Run `show bgp summary` on the AR/PE.
oliver: Running now, output:
```
Neighbor 198.51.100.1 (AS64521) established 00:03:21, flaps: 12
Prefixes received: 1500 -> sudden withdraws
Neighbor 203.0.113.2 (AS64444) established 02:12:11, flaps: 0
```
oliver: So primary upstream (64521) is unstable. Traffic is being hashed to backup (64444) which has higher latency for certain customers.
emma: Impact: 10% of EU requests see degraded latency >1s, 3% 5xx spikes in last 10m. Cust-success says 25 paying customers pinged; 4 reported sustained errors.
cust-success: AcmeCorp, NovaRetail, TwoEyes, and DigiForms reported. AcmeCorp is high-priority (SLA). They're seeing 40% request failures during surge.
raj: Escalating to provider. @net-ops open ticket with 64521, include dump, flaps, and asking for immediate stabilization or filtering. Also request emergency patch to stop withdrawing prefixes.
net-ops: Ticket created: REF #NT-2359. Sent bgp logs and pcap. Provider acknowledged and investigating. Estimated initial response 10m.
emma: Mitigation options:
- Shift critical traffic to dedicated egress in eu-central (fast failover, needs routing tweak)
- Temporarily advertise more-specific prefixes via backup transit to steer critical customers
- Increase retries and shorten client-side timeouts for some API routes (app-level)
Which do we want to execute now?
oliver: Quickest: announce more-specifics out via AS64444 to steer traffic proactively for impacted prefixes. I can prep the route advertisement now. Need approval to apply.
raj: Approve. Push more-specific /24s for the few impacted frontend ranges, only for 15m.
marta: Also push customer comms for AcmeCorp: short note that we're investigating and mitigating. I'll draft and send.
cust-success: Thanks. We'll keep them updated every 10m.
emma: Executing prep: applying route-maps and communities to announce via 203.0.113.2 (backup). Command:
```
configure terminal
route-map ANNOUNCE-MORE-SPEC permit 10
 match ip address prefix-list IMPACTED
 set community 64444:9999 no-export
ip prefix-list IMPACTED seq 5 permit 203.0.113.0/24
end
```
emma: Applied, advertising more-specifics now. Monitoring BGP table and customer connectivity.
oliver: Confirmed: /24s present in global table via 203.0.113.2. Start curl/lb checks.
```
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" https://eu.api.redwood-inference.com/health --resolve eu.api.redwood-inference.com:443:203.0.113.55
200 0.24
```
oliver: Health checks improved on the backup path.
raj: Good. net-ops, keep provider ticket open. If upstream stabilizes, we'll withdraw more-specifics and fail back gracefully.
net-ops: Provider responded: intermittent interface flaps on their spine, hardware swap planned. They requested we keep backups steered for 20m. ETA for fix 25m.
emma: Monitoring metrics: egress packet loss at azc-egress-1 dropped from 6.2% -> 0.4% after steering. Overall 5xx rate down from 3% -> 0.6%.
marta: Sent interim customer comms to impacted list, including AcmeCorp. Notifying that traffic was temporarily steered and we expect normal service once provider confirms.
cust-success: AcmeCorp acknowledged and appreciates the quick mitigation. We'll update them once provider confirms.
raj: Action items:
- net-ops: track provider fix and confirm stable BGP for 30m after last flap
- oliver/emma: prepare withdraw plan to revert announcements and validate route convergence
- marta/cust-success: follow-up msgs and post-incident summary
- oncall: keep paging open until stable
emma: I'll hold the withdraw. If provider confirms stabilization and no flaps for 30m, we'll withdraw more-specifics at 2359033723.
incident-bot: Incident P1 created: INC-2026-2359. State: Mitigated -> monitoring. Pager silence enabled for oncall. Timeline and notes will be auto-compiled.
net-ops: Provider update: hardware swap completed, no additional flaps in last 12m per their telemetry. Keep monitoring.
oliver: Running final checks across azc and eu-central. No elevated RTOs, BGP sessions stable.
emma: Withdrawing the /24 more-specifics now, reverting to normal path.
```
configure terminal
no ip prefix-list IMPACTED
no route-map ANNOUNCE-MORE-SPEC
end
```
emma: Withdrawn. BGP converging back to primary; will watch for any regression.
oliver: Final health checks:
```
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" https://eu.api.redwood-inference.com/health
200 0.21
```
emma: Metrics stable. 5xx ~0.1%, egress loss <0.2% across AZC.
marta: Sent final note to impacted customers summarizing cause (upstream transit hardware flaps), mitigation (temporary traffic steering to backup transit), and next steps.
cust-success: AcmeCorp closed their open ticket, thanks team.
raj: Postmortem owner? @emma please file a short incident postmortem with timeline, RCA (upstream interface hardware flaps, insufficient upstream redundancy for certain paths), and follow-ups: better upstream SLA, longer BGP hold timers, automatic steering runbook.
emma: Taking PM. Will post postmortem and runbook updates. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-2359 marked Mitigated -> monitoring. Closing page. Logs and timeline exported to /incidents/INC-2026-2359/ for review.
